ko.label: Capital controls on personal wealth
ko.explanation: IMF 2025 Article IV lists capital flow measures with thresholds or RBF approval (offshore investment by individuals "remains suspended"); RBF Exchange Control Guidelines (1 Jan 2026) give foreign-passport holders quotas: sale of shares/assets up to FJD 250,000 a year, non-resident transfers to own account up to FJD 250,000 per family a year, family transfers FJD 2,000 per applicant, tax clearance above FJD 20,000.

data.name: Fiji
data.summary: Fiji taxes residents' capital gains on worldwide assets at a flat 10% capital gains tax (CGT), with foreign tax credit; gains on shares listed on the South Pacific Stock Exchange are exempt. Dividends have been exempt from income tax since 1 August 2017 (FRCS); whether this also covers foreign dividends is not confirmed. No inheritance, gift or wealth tax was found; transfers on death are CGT-deferred. Resident income tax rates run to 39% above FJD 1 million (from 2024).

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Residents taxed on worldwide income (0-39%) and on worldwide capital gains at 10% CGT; dividends exempt.
regimes.eligibility: Tax residence under the Income Tax Act 2015 (commonly reported as 183 days in a 12-month period or domicile; test not checked against the Act).

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains tax of 10% applies to gains on disposal of capital assets by Fiji residents regardless of where the asset is located, including shares, securities and real property; a foreign tax credit is available for tax paid abroad on foreign capital assets. Gains on shares listed on the South Pacific Stock Exchange (SPSE) are exempt.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Resident individuals and Fiji citizens: gains up to FJD 30,000 exempt; first residential property or principal place of residence exempt; SPSE-listed shares exempt; shares held since before 1 May 2011 exempt; assets of a deceased estate disposed of within 2 years of death exempt.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: From 1 August 2025 (Income Tax (Budget Amendment) Act No. 9 of 2025) share buy-backs, redemptions, liquidations and reorganisations no longer give a tax-free deemed dividend; the gain is CGT (or income if on revenue account). CGT return due within 30 days of each disposal (except SPSE shares).

open_questions: The Income Tax Act 2015 itself (PacLII) could not be opened (HTTP 403); rules taken from FRCS guidance.

Whether a gift of shares to a child outside the family-member deferral (principal residence, first home, 'interests in capital assets between family members') is a taxable disposal at market value was not verified.
capital_gains.rate_basis: FRCS CGT page: 'a tax levied at 10% on profits or gains realized from the disposal of capital assets'; residents taxed on gains 'regardless of the asset's location'. Domestic listed = SPSE shares (exempt) = 0. Foreign listed shares, private company shares and real estate = 10% (before foreign tax credit).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Assets held as trading stock or on revenue account are outside CGT and taxed as income at up to 39%.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide for residents; credit for foreign tax paid on foreign capital assets. Non-residents are taxed only on Fiji assets.

dividends.summary: FRCS Practice Statement 39/2017 states that from 1 August 2017 dividends paid to residents and non-residents are exempt from income tax (Part 5 of the Income Tax (Exempt Income) Regulations: 'all dividends are exempt from taxation'). Fiji-company dividends are therefore 0%. The exemption is worded generally ('all dividends'), so foreign dividends appear exempt too, but no FRCS text addressing foreign-source dividends was found: low confidence on the foreign rate.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Resident individual income tax from 1 January 2024: 0% to FJD 30,000; 18% to 50,000; 20% to 270,000; then 33%-38% bands; 39% above FJD 1,000,000 (Social Responsibility Tax folded into the brackets). Unchanged in the 2025-26 and 2026-27 budgets.
dividends.important_exceptions: 2025-26 budget removed deemed-dividend treatment of capital returns on buy-backs, redemptions and liquidations (now CGT).

open_questions: Confirm in the Income Tax (Exempt Income) Regulations 2016 Part 5 (as amended 2017) that foreign-source dividends of resident individuals are exempt.
An FRCS FAQ page (2017) still says dividends are exempt only if paid from profits taxed at corporate level; it appears to predate the August 2017 change.
dividends.rate_basis: PS 39/2017 para 6 and note (1): with effect from 1 August 2017 all dividends are exempt. 'Dividend' is defined by reference to a distribution of profits by a 'company', which includes foreign bodies, so foreign dividends = 0 (low confidence). If foreign dividends were instead ordinary income, the rate would be up to 39%.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No dividend withholding since 1 August 2017 (dividends exempt for non-residents as well).
dividends.treaty_network: Small network (Australia, NZ, UK, Singapore, Malaysia, Korea, PNG and others reported; not verified). No US treaty: US dividends bear 30% US WHT, a final cost.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax and no recurring levy on financial assets.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal councils levy property rates on land in their areas (not researched).

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax was found. Estate and gift duties were discontinued by a 1985 amendment act (reported; PacLII text could not be opened). Transfers on death to an executor or beneficiary are deferred for CGT (no gain recognised; the heir takes over the cost base), and assets sold by the estate within 2 years of death are exempt.

open_questions: Primary source for abolition of estate and gift duty not opened (PacLII blocked).
Stamp Duties Act repealed from 1 August 2020 (reported); whether any transfer charge applies to inherited land not verified.
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax found. Gifts of principal residences, first residential properties or 'interests in capital assets between family members' are CGT-deferred; other gifts may be CGT disposals.
inheritance.foreign_assets: No Fiji inheritance tax on any assets (as found).

residency.tax_residency_test: Income Tax Act 2015 residence test (183 days in a 12-month period, or domicile/permanent place of abode, as commonly reported; not verified against the Act). Residents are taxed on worldwide income and gains.

routes.requirements: Not researched. Fiji has no residence-by-investment tax regime for wealthy arrivals as far as checked.

corporate.summary: FRCS states the corporate income tax rate was increased with effect from 1 August 2023 (widely reported as 25%, from 20%), but the rate was not seen in an official source in this session. Company dividends exempt from 1 August 2017. Tax-free region incentives exist.

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain subject to US federal income, estate and gift tax on worldwide income and assets wherever they live; the app adds the federal layer. Where local tax on portfolio income is nil there is nothing to credit against US tax. Fiji's 10% CGT on foreign gains is creditable against US tax on the same gain in principle; no US-Fiji treaty.
open_questions: Westpac (July 2026) reports the 2026-27 budget left personal and corporate income tax rates unchanged; the 2026-27 FRCS budget guideline was not read.
Residence routes for foreign investors not researched.

succession.name: Fiji
succession.summary: Fiji has no fixed share for children, but the Inheritance (Family Provision) Act lets a court order provision for family left too little. Trusts exist under the Trustee Act. No private foundation law was found and the Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
succession.family_claims: Inheritance (Family Provision) Act (Cap. 61 in the revised edition, as cited in case law): court may order provision for dependants and family. Estates are administered under the Succession, Probate and Administration Act 1970 (Cap. 60).
succession.foreign_law_note: No choice-of-law statute was sourced. Fiji follows English common-law conflict rules (land by location, movables by domicile); not verified from a source here.
succession.trust_note: Trustee Act (cited as Cap. 65 / Trustee Act 1966) and Public Trustee Act. Foreign trusts are recognised under common law; no trust tax regime was sourced. No private foundation law was found.
